title: Felix Holt, the Radical

vibeProfile.oneLine: An idealistic radical and a contested election in reforming England.

summary: Set around a contested election in the years of England's expanding franchise, George Eliot's political novel follows the idealistic working-class radical Felix Holt, the compromised heir Harold Transome, and the young woman caught between their worlds. Denser and less read than her masterpieces, it is a serious meditation on reform, class and the gap between political rhetoric and real change. For readers who love Eliot's moral seriousness, it rewards patience with rich characterisation and thought.
whyReadIt: Eliot's underread political novel about reform and class. Dense, serious and rewarding for her devotees.

funFacts.text: Eliot wrote it as debate over extending the vote was reshaping British politics.
